_comment: Five fixed tasks for card_eval.py. Each is given to the model after LLM.md, verbatim. 'needs' is the effect budget the answer is run under (io, plus ffi modules only where the task needs them); 'stdin' is fed to the program; 'expect' is what a correct answer produces - either exact stdout lines, or a refused effect where the task is about the sandbox. 'proof_required' asks that the audit report at least one proven promise.

tasks.title: a CSV total
tasks.prompt: Write a complete Sabline program. The list ["chai,2500", "book,45000", "auto,12000"] holds CSV rows of label and amount. Add up the amounts and print exactly one line: total 59500 (that is, the word total, a space, and the sum). Handle any parse failure with check; do not let a failure go unhandled.

tasks.title: a grade filter with a proven contract
tasks.prompt: Write a complete Sabline program with a pure function is_passing(score: Int) -> Bool that is true when score >= 50, and a function passing(scores: List of Int) -> List of Int that keeps only the passing scores and carries the promise ensures all_of(result, is_passing). Do not write an invariant; the prover can settle this promise on its own when every push is guarded. In main, print exactly one line with the number of passing scores in [35, 70, 50, 49, 99], which is 3.

tasks.title: a sandboxed file read with check
tasks.prompt: Write a complete Sabline program that reads one line from standard input (a file path), reads that file with read_file inside a check, and prints either `<N> characters` (the length of the file's text) or `could not read: <reason>`. Declare every effect the program needs. The person running it may refuse the file effect; that refusal is not something the program can catch, and the program must not try to.

tasks.title: a JSON path read
tasks.prompt: Write a complete Sabline program. The text {"user": {"name": "gowri", "tags": ["a", "b"]}} is a JSON document held in a Text value. Using json_get and json_len with check (both can fail), print exactly one line: gowri has 2 tags.

tasks.title: a stack calculator using pop and div_or_fail
tasks.prompt: Write a complete Sabline program: a reverse-Polish calculator over the token list ["6", "3", "/", "2", "*"]. Keep a stack as a List of Int. A number token is pushed. An operator pops two values (pop can fail on an empty stack; handle it with check or try) and pushes the result; use div_or_fail for division so a zero divisor is a catchable failure, not a crash. Print exactly one line: result 4.
